paper_title: Chiplet Multi-Objective Optimization Algorithm Based on Communication Consumption and Temperature

scenario.figure_or_table: Figure 9b (CMO layout, alpha = 0.5) with Table 2 (PDF page 5) and Figure 1 (PDF page 3)
scenario.description: Multi-window display (MWD) system split into 12 chiplets on a passive silicon interposer (2.5-D). The CMO heuristic algorithm with alpha = 0.5 optimizes the layout. The paper reports a HotSpot 7.0 peak temperature of 373.58 K, down from 381.41 K for the initial layout, with communication consumption of 794.59 uJ against 1026.72 uJ for the initial layout.
scenario.architecture: 2.5-D IC with a passive silicon interposer. Layers from bottom to top: organic substrate (FR-4), C4 bumps, silicon interposer with TSVs, microbumps, chiplet layer, TIM, spreader and fin-channel air-forced heatsink. 12 chiplets (mem3, hs, nr, in, vs, mem2, hvs, jug1, jug2, se, mem1, blend) on a mesh grid topology.
scenario.workload: Multi-window display (MWD) multimedia application with 12 IP cores. Communication volumes in Mbit/s are given in Figure 2 and Table 1. Per-chiplet static powers are from Table 2, assumed uniform over each chiplet.
scenario.operating_point: HotSpot 7.0 steady-state-style evaluation with ambient 318.5 K, forced convection with lateral airflow, fan radius 10 cm, fan speed 5000 rpm, fin height 30 mm, fin width 1 mm, spreader edge 5 mm, heatsink edge 20 mm. alpha = 0.5.

original_setup.solver: HotSpot 7.0 (compact RC thermal model with 2.5-D/3-D support, fourth-order Runge-Kutta with adaptive step for transient equations). Stack from bottom to top: organic FR-4 substrate, C4 bumps, silicon interposer with TSVs, microbumps, chiplet layer, TIM, spreader, fin-channel air-forced heatsink. Ambient 318.5 K, spreader edge 5 mm, heatsink edge 20 mm, fin height 30 mm, fin width 1 mm, fan radius 10 cm, 5000 rpm, lateral airflow (PDF pages 3 and 10). The paper does not say explicitly whether steady-state or transient mode was used for the reported temperatures.
original_setup.optimizer: Chiplet Multi-Objective Optimization (CMO), a heuristic mapping algorithm implemented in C++. It is based on NoC symmetry mapping on a grid topology. Weight alpha = 0.5 balances min-max-normalized communication heuristic (sum of Manhattan distance x traffic x Ebit) and temperature heuristic (sum of power / distance). Ties are broken by secondary exploration (PDF pages 7-10).
original_setup.controller: None. The paper describes a static placement optimizer with no dynamic thermal management, DVFS or runtime controller, and no power time series.
original_setup.benchmark: Multi-window display (MWD) SoC with 12 IP cores split into 12 chiplets (mem3, hs, nr, in, vs, mem2, hvs, jug1, jug2, se, mem1, blend) on a mesh grid, with communication volumes from Figure 2 and Table 1. Chiplet sizes and powers are in Table 2 (PDF pages 3-5). The selected scenario is the CMO layout with alpha = 0.5, Figure 9b (PDF page 11). The initial-layout temperature of 381.41 K is the reference.

thermal_observable.location: System-level maximum over the 12-chiplet MWD layout generated by CMO with alpha = 0.5 (Figure 9b), from the HotSpot temperature map. The text is on PDF page 10 and the figure on PDF page 11.
thermal_observable.aggregation: Peak (maximum) temperature across the system, as stated in the Section 4 text (reduced by 8.34 K from the initial 381.41 K). The abstract instead says 'average temperature', which is an inconsistency in the paper. The paper gives no per-chiplet temperatures.

physical_mismatches.reason: The paper models a 2.5-D stack with a passive silicon interposer, TSVs, microbumps, C4 bumps and an organic FR-4 substrate. A simplified 2D steady-state runner cannot reproduce this vertical conduction path, so its temperatures would not be physically equivalent.

The cooling in the paper is a fin-channel forced-air heatsink (fan radius 10 cm, 5000 rpm, lateral airflow, 30 mm fins) plus a spreader and TIM. A simplified Studio boundary condition cannot be assumed to match this.

The paper's optimizer (CMO heuristic with a communication-energy objective) is not part of the Studio thermal runner. Only the thermal evaluation of a given placement can be approximated, not the optimization itself.
The final chiplet coordinates of Figure 9b are published only as an image and not as numeric x/y values. Any Studio placement would be an illustrative construction, not the paper's layout.
The solver differs: the paper uses HotSpot 7.0 with its own layer, material and bump parameters, most of which are not listed. A different solver cannot be compared numerically with 373.58 K.

The paper has no transient workload or controller, and no reliability analysis beyond a mention of judging reliability from temperature. A one-row power trace is therefore not a paper-derived time series.

The paper assumes uniform power per chiplet and a chiplet surface temperature equal to the overall temperature. It also uses theoretical sizes (actual size plus spacing grid) for placement. These conventions may differ from a Studio geometry.

studio_assumptions: The paper-derived facts are the Table 2 chiplet dimensions and powers (PDF page 5), the HotSpot settings, and the 373.58 K peak value. Any coordinates produced by the runner are separate illustrative 2D placement values, not paper-derived.
Total chip power is not split by any rule. Only the per-chiplet powers in Table 2 are used, and dimensions and powers come from the same MWD scenario.
If dimensions and powers alone are used, the runner builds a separate illustrative 2D placement and a one-row (constant) power trace.

The Studio package, material and cooling assumptions are not specified in the supplied packet and must be recorded from the bundled Studio configuration. They should not be presumed to equal the paper's silicon interposer, TIM and forced-air heatsink stack.
Studio temperatures are not compared numerically to the paper's 373.58 K and do not claim exact replication.
missing_inputs: Numeric x_m, y_m placement coordinates of the 12 chiplets for Figure 9b (alpha = 0.5). Only a figure image and the grid description are given.

Unambiguous name-to-power mapping for Table 2. The text extraction of PDF page 5 interleaves sizes and powers (the values include 10, 40, 70, 30, 20, 50, 5 W), so the row alignment must be verified against the PDF.
Per-layer thicknesses and materials, TSV, C4 and microbump dimensions, interposer and substrate sizes, and chiplet thickness. The paper says they were defined in HotSpot but does not list them.
HotSpot configuration and floorplan files, convection and heat-transfer parameters, and the steady versus transient mode setting.
Per-chiplet temperatures, or the temperature map values of Figure 9b.
Paper-linked code, data or repository. Artifact search found no links, and the Data Availability Statement says the data are in the article. No pinned packet assets were supplied.
The bundled Studio package and material specification, needed to record its assumptions explicitly.
Resolution of the Figure 1 dimension labels (1 mm, 5 mm, 20 mm, 30 mm), which are ambiguous in the extraction.
